body:
Deferred one round by the devx seat (session `session_01YS2qzDAn3CpWdY7uBX9bFQ`, 2026-08-10) — recording the reason on the card per the "deferring is not shelving" rule:

**PR #7322 (#6888, `global_nav` retirement) is in flight and edits the same file** (`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/records-forms.json`), deliberately touching only the `global_nav` variant of this very item. Same-file work serializes across rounds. The regions are disjoint (this card is the empty-locations variant), but the item-level `revision` bump both changes want makes a textual collision likely.

Known trap for whoever dispatches this after #7322 merges: re-derive the item's current text from `origin/main` at dispatch time — both the probe wording and the revision number will have moved. The card's evidence and suggested fix direction (invert the probe's expected outcome to the post-objectui#3142 contract; keep the probe rather than deleting it) were verified plausible at triage and remain the right shape.

**Evidence-base limit, stated plainly:** this session has no access to the objectui repo (per dispatch), so the rewrite was verified against this repo's codification of the same contract — `packages/lint/src/validate-action-locations.ts`, whose `action-no-placement` rule exists *because* a locations-less action renders nowhere and whose docblock says so verbatim ("an action renders at a location only if it DECLARES that location … measurably inert as of objectui 17.1"), and which is also the authority for `locations: []` being a deliberate headless shape it does not flag — plus the card's verbatim `actionRendersAt` / `action-bar.tsx` quotes. `action-bar.tsx` itself was not read first-hand. The same limitation is stated in the PR body.

**Worktree note:** the dispatch container's primary checkout had the task branch checked out directly, and `git checkout` / `git switch` were blocked by the permission classifier, so isolation was obtained with `git worktree add -f /home/user/objectstack-7323 <branch>` and every edit made there — Prime Directive #11's guard satisfied.

The dev then used that as the `locations: []` specimen rather than authoring a second probe. That is the deferral note working as intended.
- **The probe was inverted, not deleted** — both halves stay runnable and now pin the two shapes the platform actually distinguishes: key absent (inert, what `action-no-placement` warns about) vs `locations: []` (deliberate headless, explicitly not flagged). The self-contradiction is resolved in the right direction: the `negative` list already encoded the post-#3142 contract, so the acceptance clause was the stale party.
- **Evidence limit stated honestly in the PR body**: no objectui access from that container, so the rewrite rests on this repo's codification (`packages/lint/src/validate-action-locations.ts` and its docblock) plus this card's verbatim `actionRendersAt` quote. Declared rather than papered over.
- `check:platform-checklist`'s one problem (`coverage.json · qa: UNCLASSIFIED`) was reproduced on a clean `origin/main` tree and is pre-existing — already filed as #7347, not this PR's.

Out-of-scope finding #7420 filed correctly (`RecalcSelectionAction`'s TSDoc still narrates the pre-#3142 rule, plausibly the origin of the checklist's claim) and annotated in the `source` entry rather than silently fixed.

Flipped ready, auto-merge armed. ⚠️ Arming returned the #6207 empty-field signature, but the queue is at **5/5 slots** right now (`pr-7415/7419/7423/7435/7436`), where a waiting PR and an armed-but-not-enqueued PR read identically — so the remedy toggle is deliberately **not** fired this round; it is re-evaluated on the next patrol once a slot frees.
